newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP buying into French car part firm Valeo - source.
newsitem.headline: CGIP buying into French car part firm Valeo - source.

text.p: French car parts maker Valeo looked certain to remain in French hands after industry sources said on Monday that a 28 percent stake in the firm cherished by national carmakers was to be bought by holding company CGIP.

There was no official confirmation but news conferences were announced for Tuesday morning by all three companies involved -- CGIP itself, Valeo and Cerus, the company belonging to Italian financier Carlo de Benedetti which holds 28 percent in Valeo.
An acquisition by CGIP of the strategic Cerus stake would be welcome news for the French government as well as carmakers Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen.
They had all been seeking ways to ensure Europe's second biggest car components maker stayed in foreign hands.

A CGIP spokeswoman contacted by Reuters would say no more than that a news conference was planned at 0730 GMT on Tuesday and the other two firms stuck to announcing news conferences of their own, at 0830 GMT and 1000 GMT respectively.
But industry sources said the news conference did indeed concern a CGIP acquisition of a Valeo stake from Cerus.

At Monday's Paris closing price of 310.8 francs, Valeo's entire share capital of nearly 70 million shares works out at 21.756 billion francs, making a 28 percent stake at that price worth 6.091 billion francs.

CGIP made it clear back in September that it wanted to wrap up a deal to buy into Valeo and since said it would raise around 3.2 billion francs through the sale of a stake in U.S. company Crown Cork and Seal.

The stake has been up for grabs for more than a year since de Benedetti first made it known he was looking to sell as he sought fresh finances for the Italian computer group Olivetti, from which he has since resigned as chairman.

News that his Cerus French holding company was ready to sell caused consternation in French car industry circles amid reports of interest from U.S. giants Delphi Automotive Systems, which belongs to General Motors, and TRW Inc.

Threats of a boycott by the French car manufacturers which are Valeo's biggest clients is thought to have discouraged any foreign bids. Among the most vociferous supporters of keeping Valeo French was PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet.

Valeo chairman Noel Goutard told Reuters in an interview last month that hw was not unheppy at the prospect of CGIP buying into the company and said he did not believe that the holding company's interest was just a political solution.
Goutard also rejected the notion that Valeo needed to link up with another car components maker to keep up with the industry's consolidation.
CGIP, Compagnie Generale d'Industrie et de Participations, previously held a stake in Valeo but sold it in 1993.

It has a string of investments in the industrial and information technology spheres and recently announced almost doubled net attributable profit of 603.5 million francs for the first half of 1996, including a one-off gain of 309 million.

Valeo's net attributable profit for the first six months of 1996 rose 4.3 percent to 656 million francs, but the company said the underlying rise was in fact 31 percent once a one-off capital gain of 130 million francs was stripped out of the results for the same period in 1995.
